findings.ref: item 9701-8.3-x009 answer versus lesson note Boltzmann distribution
findings.evidence: Pack x009 keys C: 'If a catalyst is added, peak P will be the same and Eₐ will move to the right.' The note says: 'Its lower $E_a$ threshold lies further left on the energy axis.'
findings.suggested: Correct the x009 answer key to B, which keeps the peak unchanged and moves Eₐ left.
findings.resolution: fix: The source image confirms official answer C: peak P stays the same and Ea moves left. The extracted options are shifted; do not change the key to B or alter the correct lesson note. In build/work/mcq/overrides.json under qid 9701_s23_12_q16 set stem="The diagram shows the Boltzmann distribution of energies in a gas. The gas can take part in a reaction with an activation energy, Eₐ. The gas is maintained at a constant temperature. Which statement is correct?"; set options={"A":"If a catalyst is added, peak P will be lower and Eₐ will move to the left.","B":"If a catalyst is added, peak P will be lower and Eₐ will move to the right.","C":"If a catalyst is added, peak P will be the same and Eₐ will move to the left.","D":"If a catalyst is added, peak P will be the same and Eₐ will move to the right."}; set answer="C"; set explanation="At constant temperature, adding a catalyst does not change the Boltzmann distribution, so peak P stays the same. A catalyst provides an alternative reaction mechanism with a lower activation energy, moving the Eₐ threshold to the left and increasing the proportion of molecules with sufficient energy to react. A and B incorrectly lower the peak; B and D incorrectly move Eₐ to the right."; retain image="Assets/mcq/9701_s23_12_q16.png".
